reading: Of the 83 pgEnums in src/db/schema.ts, 27 are *_status/*_stage and they sit on 42 columns; the honest finding is that the repo has two lifecycle grammars done well and one done twice. Done well: the four crew/desk sighting ledgers (roll_call_events, roll_call_crew_events, pre_departure_check_events, booking_arrival_events at schema.ts:8028/8158/8278/8359) share one append-only, newest-wins, cleared-as-undo shape with constants in src/lib/roll-call.ts and src/lib/arrival.ts, and trip_stage_events is derived by src/db/trip-stages.ts with no projection column at all. Done twice: bookings.status (schema.ts:2555) carries the seat's word and the arrival's word in one slot, 8 `.set({ status })` writers in 4 files overwrite it and only the 3 in src/db/check-in.ts append the trail, and three open issues from the same six days (#1838, #1694, #1836) are that slot disagreeing with the trail. The eleven side-effect ledgers (payment intents, media deletions, erasure obligations, integration deliveries, the send queue, backups, two promo tables, blow-out messages, checkouts, tips) spell one four-state lifecycle with 7 words for "done" and 6 column names for "when it resolved", and only 4 have a stuck reader (orders/page.tsx:207-210, settings/SettingsPage.tsx:20-21) — src/db/notifications.ts:87-94 says of the send queue "a row that gives up here is invisible on every staff screen". A state word is rendered nowhere in particular: "Boarded" is the value of 7 keys in 5 bundle files, "Checked in" of 4 keys in 4 files, 5 components branch inline on the codes, and none of the 35 src/i18n/*-labels.ts modules covers presence while readiness has 525 lines of one (src/i18n/readiness-labels.ts). Waivers keep a stored status that is a function of two sibling columns (src/db/waivers.ts:1222), nine dated facts on the row (schema.ts:6063-6234), two six-word derivations sharing four words (src/lib/waivers.ts:221 and :336), and three stores of link delivery (notification_deliveries, waiver_deliveries, five waiver_records.delivery_* columns). The departure's lifecycle is spread over status, cancelled_at, conditions_hold (17 readers), deleted_at, trip_blowouts (4), trip_stage_events and day_closeouts (6), with 40 hasSailed/hasReturned call sites and 168 status-scheduled/cancelled comparisons in src/db — but each store carries a written reason for its orthogonality (schema.ts:2143-2166, glossary "Conditions hold") and setTripStatus (src/db/trips-record.ts:718) is the one seam, so it is spread, not disagreeing. The known roadmap row "Check-in = boarding's first rung" (docs/product/features/roadmap.md:613) is half-dead: its mechanism was refused by ADR 20260907-the-counter-survives-offline decisions 4-5, while its problem moved from "check-in vs boarded" to "slot vs trail".

alreadyDone.what: The four sighting ledgers share one grammar: append-only, one row per tap, cleared as the undo, source live/offline, client_event_id, occurred_at + seq tiebreak, RETRACTION_SUPERSEDED constants spelled once, one staleness bound hoisted to src/lib/offline-events.ts (ADR 20260907 decision 3). A fifth ledger, trip_stage_events, joins it with re-tap instead of cleared.

The stage ledger has one writer, three readers and no projection column on trips; liveStageOf derives the word with a stated shelf life and a stage is never inferred from a clock. This is the model L02-1 asks bookings to follow.
booking_payment_events records every payment transition with status and previous_status from one writer — the one true one-event-per-transition ledger in the schema.
Readiness has exactly one vocabulary (Blocked / Ready) and one label module, which is the rendering standard the presence words lack.

Trip cancellation goes through one seam that stamps and clears cancelled_at with the status word, so the word and the time cannot disagree; the blow-out cascade and the minimum-seat sweep both call it.

no_show has one writer behind one gate, and ADR 20260911 removed the close-of-day sweep that would have let the seat word overwrite a sighting; the counter's counting predicates are pure and tested against the blocked-after-check-in case.

Roll call is deliberately tri-state (not a toggle) because not_boarded is a recorded statement distinct from unrecorded, and the two meanings of not_boarded by checkpoint are handled by one predicate, standingResultMeansSailed.

ideas.title: A booking's status is two lifecycles; arrival is its trail
ideas.reading: booking_status (src/db/schema.ts:2555) holds four words on two axes: booked/cancelled/no_show say whether the seat is held, checked_in says the diver arrived — SEAT_HELD_STATUSES = [booked, checked_in] (src/lib/no-show.ts:39) exists to fold the second axis back out, and 4 more files (first-booking.ts, kiosk-check-in.ts, reporting.ts, season-scale.ts) re-spell that pair by hand. Since ADR 20260907-the-counter-survives-offline, arrival has its own append-only trail booking_arrival_events (schema.ts:8359) with the same columns and newest-wins rules as roll_call_events, but decision 1 kept bookings.status as "the projection every existing reader looks at", so arrival lives in three places: the trail, the slot, and the offline snapshot's divers[].checkedIn (src/lib/offline-manifests.ts:328). Eight .set({ status }) writers touch the slot (src/db/check-in.ts x3, bookings.ts x3, no-show.ts:176, manifests.ts:1230) and only check-in.ts's three append a trail row; the other five overwrite checked_in without saying so. That is the disagreement behind three issues filed in six days: #1838 (reclaimReleasedSeat restores booked while undoBookingNoShow restores checked_in from standingArrivalStatus), #1694 (four "did this person dive" readers, two of which fall back to the trail through src/db/arrival-provenance.ts, 161 lines written to re-derive what the slot forgets), and the booking half of #1836. The counter-example is in the same repo: trip_stage_events (schema.ts:3098) has no projection column on trips, liveStageOf (src/lib/trip-stages.ts:55) derives the word, and no issue about a disagreeing stage exists. The roadmap row "Check-in = boarding's first rung" (docs/product/features/roadmap.md:613) proposes merging arrival into the departure checkpoint, which ADR 20260907 decisions 4-5 now refuse ("a second control on the roll-call row" is a listed rejected alternative) — the row's problem is real and its mechanism is dead. Removing checked_in reaches 26 non-test occurrences in 15 files, 74 files that read bookings.status at all, and 19 test/spec files.
ideas.idea: booking_status becomes the seat's word only — booked | cancelled | no_show — and seatIsHeld becomes status === "booked", deleting the four hand-spelled pairs. Arrival is derived from booking_arrival_events exactly as boarding is from roll_call_events and the stage from trip_stage_events: standingArrivalStatus moves to a dependency-free src/lib/presence.ts beside roll-call.ts, the counter, roster, Today and kiosk readers take an `arrived` field joined from the trail in the one-query-per-departure shape onTheWaterByRollCall already uses, and the offline snapshot's checkedIn is filled from the trail. A no-show, a cancel, a reclaim or a restore then touches the seat word and leaves the sighting standing — #1838 has nothing to restore and #1694's "sweep erases a sighting" cannot happen. The one evidence rule that remains — a standing roll-call result meaning sailed outranks a later desk word (#1836) — is written once in presence.ts and every "did they dive" reader calls it. ADR 20260907's consequence "keeping bookings.status and the trail written in one transaction" is retired by a superseding ADR that keeps its decisions 2-5 intact. The grammar afterwards: every crew or desk sighting is an append-only tap ledger with no projection, and a mutable status column says only what the shop decided (held, released, cancelled).
ideas.dissolves: The checked_in enum value, SEAT_HELD_STATUSES and its four copies, the projection half of src/db/arrival-provenance.ts, and the roadmap's "Check-in = boarding's first rung" row (superseded, not merged).
ideas.scope: src/db/schema.ts (booking_status) + one destructive migration with the H-49 line; src/db/check-in.ts, no-show.ts, manifests.ts (reclaimReleasedSeat), bookings.ts, kiosk-check-in.ts, arrival-provenance.ts, reporting.ts, season-scale.ts, first-booking.ts, executed-dives.ts, divers.ts, recap.ts, shelf.ts, today.ts; src/lib/check-in.ts, no-show.ts, manifests.ts, offline-manifests.ts, new src/lib/presence.ts; CounterQueueRow.tsx, RosterSection.tsx, OfflineManifestView.tsx, trips/[id]/manifest/page.tsx, trips/[id]/log/page.tsx; staff/checkIn.json en-US + es-ES; 19 test/spec files; glossary "Seat held", "Check-in", "Arrival event"; roadmap.md:613; a new ADR superseding decision 1 of 20260907; the export bundle's bookings.csv status column.
ideas.firstSlice: Add src/lib/presence.ts with the one derived `arrived` reader and make the five bookings.status writers outside check-in.ts stop touching arrival (closing #1838 and #1694's recap/shelf half with tests), enum value still present; the second PR drops checked_in and the four copies.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260907-the-counter-survives-offline decision 1 — supersedes its "bookings.status stays the projection" clause on the evidence of three disagreement issues in six days and H-49's ban on dual-reads, keeps decisions 2-5 (offline queue cannot say aboard) untouched; roadmap "Check-in = boarding's first rung" — retires the row, its mechanism already refused by that ADR; H-62 — answers the Check-in fold's open "arrived-vs-aboard data question"; #1838 and #1694 subsumed; #1836's booking half subsumed, its setTripStatus half untouched; ADR 20260911-the-confirm-tap-is-the-release — no_show stays the seat word, unchanged; N-53 — offline counter behaviour unchanged; settled-questions.md:41 — roll call tri-state untouched.

ideas.title: Eleven unfinished-work ledgers speak one attempt grammar
ideas.reading: Eleven tables record an external side-effect attempt — payment_operation_intents (schema.ts:5382), media_deletion_attempts (8884), processor_erasure_obligations (8962), integration_deliveries (5272), notification_send_queue (4262), shop_backup_deliveries (4627), trip_last_minute_promos (3534), shop_promo_codes (3603), trip_blowouts.message_status (9095), booking_checkouts (4836), tips (5086) — each with its own pgEnum, 11 of the 27 status enums. They spell the same four states with four words for not-yet (pending, started, queued, owed), three for in-flight (processing, sending, started), seven for done (succeeded, sent, delivered, completed, discharged, paid, active) and two for failed (failed, expired). The resolved-time column has six spellings (resolved_at x2, discharged_at, delivered_at, finished_at, completed_at x2), the error column three (error_message, last_error x4, error_code x2), the counter three (attempts x3, attempt_count, recovery_attempts). Each was copied on purpose and by hand: media_deletion_attempts says "Mirrors paymentOperationIntents (CR-005)" (schema.ts:8888) and trip_last_minute_promos "mirroring startBookingCheckout's insert-before-external-call shape" (3541). "Is this stuck?" is answered by four bespoke readers (listStuckPaymentOperations, listPendingMediaDeletions, listOwedProcessorErasures, listOwedShopCancellationRefunds) on two surfaces (orders/page.tsx:207-210, settings/SettingsPage.tsx:20-21), and by nobody for the send queue or the integration outbox: src/db/notifications.ts:87-94 says "there is no such surface... a row that gives up here is invisible on every staff screen" (#1719, still open as #1826), and integration_deliveries gives up at attemptCount < 8 (src/db/integration-events.ts:250) with no reader. ADR 20260723-payment-operation-intents argues for insert-before-call and a human-visible stuck queue; nothing in it or its two mirrors argues for a vocabulary per table.
ideas.idea: One attempt_status enum (pending | in_flight | done | failed) and one column trio (attempts, last_error, resolved_at) on every ledger that records a side effect; the domain word survives only where it is a kind, not a state (an erasure row is owed because it is a processor_erasure with status pending). One src/lib/attempts.ts holds the staleness rule per kind (stuckAfterMs — the five-minute payment window, the send queue's three daily passes, the outbox's eight) and one src/db/unfinished.ts reader lists every row in_flight past its window or failed with attempts exhausted, tagged by kind and shop; the four bespoke readers become four kind filters over it. Each queue stays on the surface its object owns (the route map's rule — Orders, Settings' Data & integrations, never Reports), and the two ledgers with no surface today get one for free because the reader already sees them. Seeds and /api/test/seed-trouble-states write the one enum. The grammar afterwards: a ledger row is pending until a worker claims it, in_flight while a call is out, and done or failed with a reason — the same sentence on eleven tables, and a twelfth ledger inherits it instead of inventing an eighth word for done.
ideas.dissolves: Ten of the eleven attempt-status enums, six spellings of "when it resolved", three of "what went wrong", four hand-written stuck readers, and the silent give-up in the send queue and the integration outbox.
ideas.scope: src/db/schema.ts (11 tables) + one migration; src/db/payment-operations.ts, media-deletions.ts, processor-erasure.ts, integration-events.ts, notifications.ts, backup delivery writer, trip-promos.ts, shop-promos.ts, blowouts.ts, checkouts.ts, tips.ts, refunds.ts; new src/lib/attempts.ts and src/db/unfinished.ts; orders/page.tsx, settings/SettingsPage.tsx, the integrations settings page, Today's urgency:now row; seed-front-desk.ts and /api/test/seed-trouble-states; staff bundle queue words en-US + es-ES; ADRs 20260723-payment-operation-intents, 20260723-media-validation-and-deletion, 20260720-notification-attempt-history, 20260804-blowout-cascade amended by one new ADR; glossary.
ideas.firstSlice: Add src/lib/attempts.ts and src/db/unfinished.ts reading the existing eleven enums through a per-kind mapping, and put the send queue's parked rows on Settings' Data & integrations (closing #1826) — no schema change; the enum collapse is the second slice, one ledger family per PR on a stack.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260723-payment-operation-intents — extended, not reversed: the claim column, idempotency keys and the human-not-guess stance stay, started renames to in_flight; ADR 20260720-notification-attempt-history and 20260804-blowout-cascade — their words change, their send-once rules do not; #1826 and #1719 subsumed (the parked-failure surface); #1865 touched (a provider error is worded in one place); route map "back-office queues live with the object, never on Reports" — kept; roadmap "One Bill per booking" — adjacent (checkouts and tips keep their money meaning, only their attempt words change).

ideas.title: Presence has one word list, rendered from one derived state
ideas.reading: "Boarded" is the value of 7 different keys in 5 bundle files (staff/manifest.json:20 and :146, checkIn.json:15, shared.json:347, :371 and :462, diver.json:2466); "Checked in" of 4 keys in 4 files (trips.json:401, manifest.json:96, checkIn.json:25, shared.json:397); "Not here" appears in 4 strings (manifest.json:98, checkIn.json:41-42, shared.json:363). Five components branch inline on the codes (=== "boarded", "checked_in", "no_show"): CounterQueueRow.tsx, RosterSection.tsx, OfflineManifestView.tsx, trips/[id]/manifest/page.tsx, trips/[id]/log/page.tsx. src/i18n has 35 *-labels.ts modules — readiness-labels.ts alone is 525 lines — and a grep for a label module naming boarded, checked_in or arrived returns 0 files. The codes live in three modules with three shapes: RollCallState awaiting|boarded|not_boarded (src/lib/roll-call.ts:25), ArrivalStatus arrived|cleared (src/lib/arrival.ts:25), and the booking words checked_in|no_show (schema.ts:2555) — plus two qualifiers that change the sentence but are not states, self-reported (src/db/arrival-provenance.ts:59) and missingAfterDive (src/db/manifests.ts:1225). ADR 20260907 decision 5 argues that each row must "say the act in words" so the wrong list cannot be tapped — an argument for one careful word per state, which seven keys for "Boarded" do not give.
ideas.idea: One derived Presence type in src/lib/presence.ts (dependency-free like roll-call.ts, so the service worker shares it): expected | self_reported | arrived | boarded | not_boarded | missing_after_dive | released — the union of the desk's and the rail's answers about one person on one departure, parameterised by checkpoint. One src/i18n/presence-labels.ts maps each state to exactly one key per locale (the word, the pill, the aria phrase), and the five components, Today's departure rows, the offline view and the diver's "Aboard · {when}" line render through it. The rail and the desk keep separate controls — ADR 20260907's structural refusal stands, because presence is read through this type and never written through it; what merges is the reading. Afterwards a state word is spelled once in English and once in Spanish, a new surface that draws a boat cannot invent an eighth "Boarded", and pnpm check:copy's baseline falls by the deleted keys.
ideas.dissolves: Seven keys for one word, five inline code-to-word branches, and the three-module split of the presence vocabulary on the read side.
ideas.scope: src/lib/presence.ts (new, shared with L02-1), src/i18n/presence-labels.ts (new); staff/manifest.json, checkIn.json, shared.json, trips.json, diver.json in en-US and es-ES; the five components plus today rows and the diver's trip line; e2e/visual.spec.ts captures of counter, manifest and roster; glossary "Check-in", "Boarding", "No-show" cross-links; docs/design/surfaces.md's counter entry.
ideas.firstSlice: Add presence-labels.ts and route the manifest's and the counter's pills through it, deleting the duplicate keys those two surfaces owned; the remaining surfaces follow in the same stack.
ideas.conflicts: Composes with L02-1 (shares presence.ts) but does not require it; ADR 20260907 decision 5 — kept, controls stay separate; ADR 20260828-a-missing-diver-gets-a-sentence — the note stays beside the word, not inside it; #1840 (offline roll-call control) and #1690 (withholding an unconfirmed identity on the manifest) touch the same rows and should land on this type; H-71 (b) "every page title becomes the tab's word" is the same instinct one level up.

ideas.title: A waiver's standing is derived once; its stored status is history
ideas.reading: waiver_records.status (schema.ts:6026) is three words, and its only non-paper writer sets it as a function of a sibling column: medicalReviewRequired ? "medical_review" : "completed" (src/db/waivers.ts:1222), while pending is the default, i.e. completed_at is null. Beside it sit nine lifecycle timestamps on the same row (started_at, consented_at, signed_at, completed_at, superseded_at, medical_cleared_at, medical_clearance_declined_at, guardian_consented_at, guardian_signed_at at schema.ts:6063-6234) and expires_at. Two derivations turn the row into a word: WaiverState (6 values, src/lib/waivers.ts:336) for one record and ShopWaiverStatus (6 states, :221) for a person — they share four words and each has two the other lacks (not_sent/awaiting_signature vs none/guardian_missing), so a minor's solo signature is complete in one vocabulary and guardian_missing in the other. waiverState's own comment concedes the split: "The record keeps saying medical_review because that is what happened to it" (waivers.ts:349-351) — the stored word is history, the derived word is standing. Link delivery is stored three ways: notification_deliveries per booking and purpose (schema.ts:4089), waiver_deliveries per channel (6352, ADR 20260820-waiver-delivery-is-per-channel), and five waiver_records.delivery_* columns (6028-6032) written only by the independent-waiver branch (src/db/notifications.ts:865-880 and :1165). That ADR rejected collapsing the columns "on blast radius rather than principle" and wrote the escape hatch ("collapse it into waiver_deliveries and drop the columns") five days after H-49 (2026-08-15) said blast radius on pre-pilot data is not a reason.
ideas.idea: Drop waiver_records.status and read the row's standing from its timestamps through one derivation, waiverStanding(record, { signer, templateVersion, now }), that replaces both WaiverState and ShopWaiverStatus with one word list: none | sent | awaiting_signature | signed | expired | superseded | medical_review | medical_not_cleared | guardian_missing. The booking-scoped and person-scoped readers (effectiveWaiverForBooking, shopWaiverStatus) become two selectors over the same standing rather than two vocabularies, and readiness, the diver record, the counter, close-out, the recap and the export all ask it. Delivery moves into waiver_deliveries alone — the independent-waiver branch writes a row where it now writes five columns, and the webhook's fallback keys on that table — taking the ADR's own escape hatch under H-49. Afterwards a waiver is a signed evidence row whose every state is a dated fact, "what does this waiver say now" has one answer everywhere it is asked, and no column can disagree with the timestamp that implies it.
ideas.dissolves: The waiver_record_status enum, one of the two derived unions, and the five record-level delivery columns.
ideas.scope: src/db/schema.ts (waiver_records) + one destructive migration with the H-49 line; src/lib/waivers.ts, src/lib/readiness.ts, src/lib/guardian.ts; src/db/waivers.ts, notifications.ts (independent branch and the :1165 webhook update), anonymize.ts:692, export.ts (waiver_records.csv shape) and export.test.ts; src/i18n/waiver-labels.ts and the waiver words in diver.json and staff bundles en-US + es-ES; ADR 20260820-waiver-delivery-is-per-channel superseded on the columns; glossary waiver entries; e2e waiver specs.
ideas.firstSlice: Replace waiverState and ShopWaiverStatus with one waiverStanding behind the existing callers with tests pinned (no schema change); the column drops and the delivery-row move are the second PR.
ideas.conflicts: ADR 20260820-waiver-delivery-is-per-channel — takes its stated escape hatch, keeps the per-channel table; ADR 20260907-guardian-co-signature — guardian_missing stays a state; H-02 — retention of waiver evidence unchanged, the timestamps are the evidence; H-49 — the reason the blast-radius argument no longer holds; #1855 (identity-unconfirmed blocker copy) adjacent, not subsumed.
